title: Introducing the NoAI & CreatedWithAI Tags
quote: [2023-02-20] the NoAI model tag will indicate to generative AI programs that a particular model is not to be used for generative AI data collection. [...] check the box marked Add NoAI meta tags to all uploads [...] Sketchfab agrees not to use any of your uploads in datasets for, in the development of, or as inputs to generative AI programs [...] agrees not to license any of your uploads to third parties [...] Changes took effect March 23, 2023.

title: Restricting Generative AI Use of Free Models
quote: [2023-11-21] Creators can no longer apply NoAI tags to new Creative Commons-licensed uploads [...] the CC license may allow use of the work by generative AI programs regardless of the tag [...] The NoAI tag becomes contractually enforceable on Standard-licensed models once they have been downloaded from Sketchfab [...] Standard License permits worldwide use for all types of use (whether commercial and non-commercial), in all types of derivative works. No credit needs to be given.

title: Sketchfab introduces NoAI and CreatedWithAI tags
quote: [2023-02-21] forbid any asset with the NoAI tag from being used as an input for generative AI programs, or to develop new generative AI tools [effective March 23, 2023] [...] an HTML meta tag that appears in the model webpage on the site [...] Sketchfab has not seen a comparable backlash [to ArtStation], partly because most 3D workflows do not currently rely on generative AI programs.

title: UPDATE: All Deviations Are Opted Out of AI Datasets
quote: [2022-11-11] All deviations on the platform are not authorized for inclusion in third-party datasets used to train artificial-intelligence models — unless you choose to opt in. [...] <meta name=robots content=noimageai> or <meta name=robots content=noai> [...] X-Robots-Tag: noimageai / noai [...] ensure their training data set excludes all content for which either of these directives are present

title: Noai and noimageai Tag Adoption: Study and Live Dashboard
quote: [June 2026] 88,000+ domains using noai or noimageai tags [...] Meta tag adoption: 87.8% of adopters; HTTP header: 26.7%; both: 14.5% [...] Where large AI firms offer opt-outs, they have generally done so via robots.txt crawler tokens [...] rather than honoring the noai meta tag specifically. [...] Google own robots meta specification does not list noai

title: Sketchfab & Objaverse: AI copyright dispute enters third dimension
quote: [2023-04-15] more than 800,000 3D models sourced from Sketchfab [...] all of the models that we have seen were made downloadable for free on Sketchfab under Creative Commons licenses [...] includes 3D models whose creators have set the NoAI tag, which Sketchfab introduced in February. [...] Sketchfab: They did this before us implementing the noai tag [...] We understand artists concerns and are looking into it.

title: Objaverse: A Universe of Annotated 3D Objects

title: Sketchfab mandates AI disclosure, Epic Games accounts
quote: [effective 2025-12-11] Every AI-generated model will require the CreatedWithAI label [...] New users signing up to Sketchfab must use Epic Games accounts [...] New search filters [...] will enable you to find or exclude AI-generated content [...] Sketchfab may automatically assign the CreatedWithAI label to models it detects were created with generative AI

title: Understanding CC Licenses and AI Training: A Legal Primer
quote: AI training is often permitted by copyright. This means that the CC license conditions have limited application to machine reuse. [...] using a more restrictive CC license in an effort to prevent AI training is not an effective approach

title: Introducing CC Signals: A New Social Contract for the Age of AI
quote: [2025-06-25] a new preference signals framework designed to increase reciprocity and sustain a creative commons in the age of AI [...] While CC signals may range in enforceability, legally binding in some cases and normative in others, their application will always carry ethical weight. [...] a call for a new pact between those who share data and those who use it to train AI models

title: Associating AI Usage Preferences With Content (draft-ietf-aipref-attach-02)
quote: [2025-07-21] Content-Usage [is] a structured field dictionary [...] indicates usage preferences regarding the content of the HTTP message [...] content-usage = *WS content-usage *WS : *WS [ path-pattern 1*WS ] usage-pref EOL [...] Content-Usage rules [...] determine the usage preferences for resources using the same path prefix matching rules [as Allow/Disallow]

title: TDM Reservation Protocol (TDMRep) — Final Community Group Report
authors: W3C Text and Data Mining Reservation Protocol Community Group
quote: [2024-02-02] an exception for any organisation willing to carry out TDM for any purpose other than scientific research, including commercial purposes, which applies on the condition that the use of content for TDM has not been expressly reserved by their rightsholders in an appropriate manner, such as machine-readable means. [...] tdmrep.json at /.well-known/ [...] tdm-reservation and the optional tdm-policy are two properties added to the HTTP header

title: Adversarial Perturbations Cannot Reliably Protect Artists From Generative AI
quote: [rev. 2025-02-11] only provide a false sense of security [...] image upscaling, are sufficient to create robust mimicry methods that significantly degrade existing protections [...] all existing protections can be easily bypassed, leaving artists vulnerable to style mimicry [...] tools based on adversarial perturbations cannot reliably protect artists from the misuse of generative AI

title: Getty Images v. Stability AI: English High Court Rejects Secondary Copyright Claim
quote: On 4 November 2025, the High Court of England and Wales handed down its long-awaited judgment [...] Getty accepted there was no evidence that the training and development of Stable Diffusion took place in the UK [...] the model weights are not themselves an infringing copy and they do not store an infringing copy [...] The judgment does not decide whether UK-based web scraping and model training would infringe

title: Federal Courts Find Fair Use in AI Training: Key Takeaways from Kadrey v. Meta and Bartz v. Anthropic
quote: [Bartz, 2025-06-23] exceedingly transformative [...] pirating copies to build a research library without paying for it [...] was its own use—and not a transformative one. [Kadrey, 2025-06-25] does not stand for the proposition that Meta use of copyrighted materials to train its language models is lawful. It stands only for the proposition that these plaintiffs made the wrong arguments

title: AI and copyright: The training of general-purpose AI (EPRS At a Glance, PE 769.585)
quote: [April 2025] The European AI Act has two provisions related to copyright (Article 53(1)(c) and (d)). The first requires GPAI providers to comply with copyright law and the opt-out exception of the Copyright Directive, which authorises TDM as long as rights-holders do not express their refusal [...] regardless of the jurisdiction in which the copyright-relevant acts underpinning the training [...] take place (recital 106). [...] For machine-readable, GPAI providers support the adoption of an easy-to-access standardised file such as robot.txt. A recent German court case ruled that including the opt-out in natural language – for instance in terms of use – qualifies as a machine-readable opt-out. [...] the opt-out mechanism is likely to fail whenever rights-holders do not have the administrative rights for the webpage displaying their works

title: Training and Data Mining Assertion 1.1 — Creator Assertions Working Group
quote: A training and data mining assertion SHALL have a label of cawg.training-mining. [...] cawg.data_mining, cawg.ai_inference, cawg.ai_training, cawg.ai_generative_training [...] Each entry describes whether its use is allowed, notAllowed, or constrained. [...] [earlier C2PA 1.4] used labels with the prefix c2pa. [...] In the absence of additional information, constrained shall be treated as equivalent to notAllowed.

title: LightShed: Defeating Perturbation-based Image Copyright Protections
quote: LightShed, a generalizable depoisoning attack that effectively identifies poisoned images and removes adversarial perturbations [...] achieving a TPR of 99.98% and TNR of 100% on detecting NightShade [...] a single model to recognize poisoned images [across NightShade and Glaze]

title: The EU AI Act and copyright compliance
quote: [2025-04-30] The Code commits signatories to employ the crawlers that read and follow instructions expressed in accord with the Robot Exclusion Protocol. [...] robots.txt is the most common technical protocol [for reserving rights] though it only provides guidance to compliant bots

title: RFC 9309: Robots Exclusion Protocol
quote: originally defined by Martijn Koster in 1994 [...] These rules are not a form of access authorization. [...] The Robots Exclusion Protocol is not a substitute for valid content security measures.

title: ArtStation Responds to the No to AI-Generated Images Protest
quote: [2022-12-15] We plan to add tags enabling artists to choose to explicitly allow or disallow the use of their art for training [...] We do not plan to add either of these tags by default, in which case the use of the art by AI will be governed solely by copyright law. [...] disallow the use of art by AI where the artist has chosen to disallow it

title: Commission launches consultation on protocols for reserving rights from text and data mining under the AI Act and the GPAI Code of Practice
quote: Opening: 01 December 2025 [...] Closing: 23 January 2026 [...] protocols that are state-of-the-art, technically implementable, and widely adopted by rightsholders across different cultural and creative sectors [...] Following these discussions, the Commission will publish the list of generally-agreed machine-readable opt-out solutions. This list will be reviewed regularly, at least every two years.

title: Sketchfab Terms of Use
quote: you shall not collect, aggregate, mine, scrape, or otherwise use NoAI Content (i) in datasets utilized by Generative AI Programs; (ii) in the development of Generative AI Programs [...] Sketchfab agrees that it will not use your User Content or license your User Content to third parties for use (i) in datasets utilized by Generative AI Programs [...] If you make User Content available and such User Content is created using Generative AI Programs, you must label such User Content as CreatedWithAI

title: Machine-Readable opt-outs and AI training: Hamburg Court clarifies copyright exceptions
quote: [OLG Hamburg 5 U 104/24, 2025-12-10] Rights holders can block TDM uses, but only if the opt-out is expressed in a machine-readable format. [...] General terms of use or human-readable disclaimers are insufficient. [...] Implement machine-readable opt-outs (robots.txt, TDM Reservation Protocol, metadata tags). [...] Downloading and analysing images to validate image-text pairs is covered by the TDM exception, even if this occurs before actual model training.
